title: Opening matn definition
arabic: وهي رئاسة عامة في أمر الدين والدنيا خلافة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، وأحكامه في الفروع. إلا أنه لما شاعت من أهل البدع اعتقادات فاسدة مخلة بكثير من القواعد أدرجت مباحثها في الكلام.
english: It is general leadership in religious and worldly affairs in succession to the Prophet, blessings and peace be upon him. Its rulings belong among practical legal matters. But because corrupt beliefs from the proponents of innovation became widespread, undermining many principles, its investigations were incorporated into kalām.
notes: The digital witness has وأحكامه (masculine pronoun); this wording is preserved. The antecedent and a possible reading وأحكامها should be checked against print. This excerpt is not evidence that the whole printed matn has been recovered.

title: Opening matn of Investigation One
arabic: نصب الإمام واجب على الخلق سمعا عندنا وعند عامة المعتزلة، وعقلا عند بعضهم، وعلى الله عند الشيعة، وليس بواجب أصلا عند النجدات، وحال ظهور العدل عند الأصم، والظلم عند القوطي. لنا وجوه: الأول الإجماع حتى قدموه على دفن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم. الثاني أنه لا يتم إلا به ما وجب من إقامة الحدود وسد الثغور ونحو ذلك مما يتعلق بحفظ النظام. الثالث أن فيه جلب منافع ودفع مضار لا تحصى، وذلك واجب إجماعا. فإن قيل: ويتضمن مضارا أيضا، قلنا: لا يعبأ بها لقلتها. فإن قيل: فالأئمة بعد الأئمة المهديين على الضلالة، قلنا: ضرورة فلا معصية ولا ضلالة. الرابع وجوب طاعته ومعرفته بالكتاب والسنة، وهو يقتضي وجوب حصوله وذلك نصبه.
english: Appointing an imam is an obligation upon people established by revelation, according to us and the generality of the Muʿtazila; according to some of them, it is established by reason. According to the Shiʿa it is an obligation upon God. It is not obligatory at all according to the Najadāt; nor, according to al-Aṣamm, when justice prevails; nor, according to al-Fuwaṭī, when oppression prevails. We have several arguments. First, consensus: they even gave it precedence over the Prophet’s burial. Second, the obligatory implementation of prescribed punishments, defence of the frontiers, and similar matters pertaining to the preservation of order cannot be achieved without it. Third, it brings benefits and averts harms beyond reckoning, and that is obligatory by consensus. If it is objected that it also involves harms, we reply that they are too few to count against it. If it is objected that the imams after the rightly guided imams are therefore in error, we reply that this is a situation of necessity, so there is neither sin nor error. Fourth, the Book and the Sunna make obedience to and recognition of the imam obligatory; this requires that he exist, which is brought about by appointing him.
notes: The short answer ضرورة is expanded in English only to the extent needed for grammar; the commentary gives the fuller distinction between voluntary omission and inability. The name al-Fuwaṭī is represented in the electronic Arabic as القوطي.
